logline: A librarian in a stalling long-term relationship falls for a single-father pharmacist, and the two slowly, honestly negotiate love against a backdrop of social expectation and family pressure.

renewal.note: 32-episode run (structured as 16 pairs of 35-minute episodes) completed July 2019. Directed by Ahn Pan-seok, written by Kim Eunsang. No continuation.

bollymeter.basis: RT Tomatometer 94% from 3 critics. IMDb 7.9/10. Critics at Decider and But Why Tho praised its portrait of adult romance under societal pressure; some noted the deliberate pacing requires patience.

pull_quotes.text: A really interesting look at how romance in your 30s, no matter where you live, is complicated as hell.
One Spring Night is also about female solidarity, and women who are supportive of each other.

seasons.review_body: One Spring Night aired on MBC from May to July 2019, the network's first weekday miniseries in the earlier 20:55 KST slot, and drew a 9.5% viewership rating for its finale. Director Ahn Pan-seok and writer Kim Eunsang - the same creative team behind Something in the Rain - applied a similarly patient, naturalistic approach to adult romance. Han Ji-min and Jung Hae-in's chemistry was widely praised, and critics flagged the show's unusually honest treatment of single parenthood stigma in Korean society. The Rotten Tomatoes Tomatometer sits at 94% from a small critic sample of three. Joel Keller at Decider called it 'a really interesting look at how romance in your 30s is complicated as hell.' The 32-episode run, structured as short paired episodes, rewards viewers willing to let the drama build slowly.

episode_reviews.title: Episode 1
episode_reviews.spoiler_free: A quiet, observational opener that establishes the librarian's comfortable but airless relationship before introducing the pharmacist as a disruption - gentle and sure-footed in its setup.
episode_reviews.the_moment: The first wordless moment of recognition between the two leads in the pharmacy - nothing dramatic, just two people noticing each other in a way neither expected.

critic_note.text: A really interesting look at how romance in your 30s, no matter where you live, is complicated as hell.

episode_reviews.title: Episode 32
episode_reviews.spoiler_free: The finale resolves its central tension without melodrama, trusting that the accumulation of small honest moments across 32 episodes has earned the ending. The 9.5% finale rating suggests audiences agreed.
episode_reviews.the_moment: The final conversation between the leads strips away every social obstacle the series spent weeks building, leaving only the choice each person has to make for themselves.
